definitions.explanation: A count of seven people, using the Sino-Japanese number with the counter {人|にん}. Also read ななにん, which is now more common in speech.

examples.japanese: この{班|はん}は{七人|しちにん}のメンバーで{構成|こうせい}されている。
examples.english: This group is made up of seven members.

examples.japanese: {黒澤|くろさわ}{監督|かんとく}の『{七人|しちにん}の{侍|さむらい}』は、{世界中|せかいじゅう}の{映画|えいが}に{影響|えいきょう}を{与|あた}えた。
examples.english: Director Kurosawa's Seven Samurai influenced films around the world.

notes:
{七|しち} plus the counter {人|にん} for people.

WHICH READING:
Both しちにん and ななにん are correct. ななにん is preferred in speech because しち is easily misheard as {一|いち}, but fixed titles and set phrases keep しちにん.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {七人|しちにん}で: as a group of seven
- {七人|しちにん}{兄弟|きょうだい}: seven siblings
- {七人|しちにん}の{侍|さむらい}: Seven Samurai (the 1954 film)

RELATED COUNTS:
- {六人|ろくにん}: six people
- {八人|はちにん}: eight people
- {何人|なんにん}: how many people
